title: Claude Fable 5 & the Mythos Class
content:
## Overview

On June 9, 2026, Anthropic released **Claude Fable 5** — the first model from a new tier it calls the "Mythos class," which sits above Opus in capability. Alongside it came **Claude Mythos 5**, the same underlying model with some safeguards lifted, available only to a narrow group of cyber defenders and critical infrastructure providers.

Fable 5 is the most capable model Anthropic has made broadly available, achieving state-of-the-art results on nearly every benchmark the company tested.

---

## Technical Specifications

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Context window | 1,000,000 tokens |
| Max output tokens | 128,000 |
| Adaptive thinking | Always-on |
| Input cost | $10 / 1M tokens |
| Output cost | $50 / 1M tokens |
| API model ID | `claude-fable-5` |

Both Fable 5 and Mythos 5 share the same pricing and context window.

---

## Benchmark Performance

Fable 5 leads on a wide range of benchmarks at the time of release:

| Benchmark | Fable 5 | Previous best |
|---|---|---|
| SWE-Bench Pro | **80.3%** | ~69.2% (Opus 4.8) |
| Harvey BigLaw Bench | **93.4%** | — (new high) |
| Databricks OfficeQA Pro | **57.9%** | — (new SOTA) |

The SWE-Bench Pro gap of ~11 percentage points over the next-best model (Opus 4.8) is one of the largest single-generation capability jumps in the Claude family.

---

## Always-On Adaptive Thinking

Unlike earlier models where extended thinking was an optional API parameter, Fable 5 runs **adaptive thinking continuously**. The model allocates its own reasoning budget per request — faster for straightforward queries, deeper for complex multi-step problems. Developers cannot disable it, but they can influence behavior through system prompting.

This design is part of what Anthropic calls the "Mythos-class" architecture: the model is built to hold focus across millions of tokens and to improve its own work using notes it accumulates during long-running tasks.

---

## Safety Architecture: Fallback to Opus 4.8

Fable 5 includes automated safety classifiers that monitor outputs in real time. For requests touching sensitive domains — including cybersecurity exploitation, biology, and certain chemistry topics — the system automatically falls back to **Claude Opus 4.8** for that response.

According to Anthropic, fewer than 5% of sessions trigger a fallback. The fallback model is noted in response metadata, so applications can detect which model actually served the request.

This two-model architecture means a call to `claude-fable-5` may occasionally return an Opus 4.8 response, by design.

---

## Claude Mythos 5

Mythos 5 is the same underlying model as Fable 5 with some safety guardrails reduced, intended for organizations with a verified defensive mandate. Access is not available via the standard API and requires direct approval from Anthropic. Initial access is limited to:

- Critical infrastructure security teams (energy, finance, transportation)
- Vetted cybersecurity research firms conducting authorized red-team work

For most developers and enterprises, **Claude Fable 5 is the practical frontier model**.

---

## Comparison to Earlier Claude Generations

| Model | SWE-Bench Pro | Context | Release |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude 3.5 Sonnet | ~49% | 200K | Jun 2024 |
| Claude Opus 4.7 | ~64.3% | 200K | Apr 2026 |
| Claude Opus 4.8 | 69.2% | 1M | May 2026 |
| **Claude Fable 5** | **80.3%** | **1M** | Jun 2026 |

---

## Developer Notes

- **Model ID:** `claude-fable-5`
- **Availability:** General API (claude.ai and direct API)
- **Long-context use cases:** The 1M token context makes Fable 5 practical for full-codebase analysis, large document review, and multi-session memory stored directly in context.
- **Agentic workflows:** The 128K output limit enables generating larger code files, longer structured reports, and more comprehensive tool-call sequences in a single response turn.
